correctness.rationale: The n independent uniform circular points yield Dirichlet(1,...,1) spacings after a rotation. The affine translation probability of k simultaneous specified threshold exceedances is exactly (1-sum thresholds)_+^(n-1). This proves every coefficient of the joint PGF and the covariance. Its positive prefactor times a strictly decreasing-then-constant scalar B(s) proves all signs and zero ranges, with nonconstant N(r) and hence strictly positive variance before the critical radius; n=2,r=1/2 is explicitly degenerate. The boundary root is solved without approximations. The separate rational inversion/direct-integration checker passed 1,640 grouped assertions; finite checks are secondary to the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The exact finite-n sign phase theorem has three sharply distinguished regimes: strictly positive for all upper thresholds, a terminal zero interval at the critical lower threshold, and exactly one sign crossing below it. It is not asserted that the Dirichlet joint-volume identity or Shorack limiting covariance is novel. Full-text Lo 2014 Theorem 1 directly covers the Gaussian limit, not the exact finite covariance zero curve. Mijatović--Vysotsky 2015 treats extreme maximal spacings. Pyke 1965, Koziol 1977, and Beirlant--van Zuijlen 1985 remain material-read risks; their accessible abstracts do not conclusively exclude broader finite results, so the judgment is best-knowledge, not priority certification.

value.rationale: The threshold count is the natural empirical-survivor statistic of uniform circular spacings, relevant to multiscale spacing goodness-of-fit and extreme-gap tests. The theorem determines exactly when nested counts at two scales have opposite covariance sign, characterizes a unique crossing for every subcritical lower threshold, and identifies an exceptional critical threshold with an entire interval of exact uncorrelatedness. These are meaningful global structural facts about a classical stochastic process, not a marginal moment or arbitrary finite computation. The known asymptotic process by itself does not yield the finite boundary.
